conviction_note: Nothing decisive and unpriced turned up: GDYN has topped revenue consensus four quarters running by 0.2-1.5%, so a print near $114m against a $112.77m bar is likely, but it would land inside the company's own $112-114m guide, and the last such beat (Q2, with the FY guide held) closed -2.4%. The reaction turns on the Q4 guide and how the $435-465m FY range is narrowed; the $450m midpoint needs about $125m in Q4, the high end was tied to acquisitions, and none has been announced since May. Street FY sits near $440m, so a lower-half narrowing is mostly priced. Peer reads are mixed: Accenture strong, Infosys cut, Cognizant trimmed today. p_up is 48 on a 7% absolute move, which gives -0.28. The findings sum to -0.4. Both numbers are near zero and agree in sign.

findings.finding: GDYN has beaten revenue consensus four quarters running: Q3'25 $104.16m vs $103.74m (+0.4%), Q4'25 $106.15m vs $105.93m (+0.2%), Q1'26 $104.10m vs $103.32m (+0.8%), Q2'26 $108.16m vs $106.55m (+1.5%, above the top of its own $106-108m guide). The Q3 consensus of $112.77m sits below the $113m guide midpoint, so the same pattern puts revenue near $114m, about +1% vs the bar. That is still inside the company's $112-114m guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: +1.5% revenue beat with the FY guide held, closed -2.41% (MarketBeat had it down 7.4% intraday on 2026-07-31). Q1'26: +0.8% beat, +2.11%. Q3'25: +0.4% beat, +22.89%, but that print came with a guide raise and a new $50m buyback (authorized 2025-10-23).
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (undated page; Q3'26 preview listing reported vs estimate for the last four quarters)
findings.why_not_priced: A small habitual beat is mostly priced: the bar sits inside the guide and every terminal shows the beat history. If the market expected more, the consensus would sit at the top of the $112-114m range rather than below the midpoint, and it does not.
findings.independence: Q2 10-Q/8-K shows the Q2 beat above the top of the range (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/GDYN/8-k-grid-dynamics-holdings-inc-reports-material-event-d841ff0e3f46.html). Shares the consensus history with the bar; it is one company-level pattern, not two.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of $435-465m, reaffirmed 2026-07-30, has a $450m midpoint. With H1 at $212.3m and Q3 at a $113m midpoint, that needs about $124.7m in Q4, +10% q/q. Management (Doradla, Q2 call) tied the move to the high end to working days, billable headcount and acquisitions. No acquisition has been announced since Ekumen closed on 2026-05-19 ($18.4m, revenue 'de minimis'): no 8-K since 2026-07-30 and no press release in Aug-Oct. So the FY range is likely narrowed into the lower half, where the street's roughly $440m (implied Q4 about $115m) already sits. The risk is a Q4 guide below about $115m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven prints moved most: 2025-07-31 -16.44% (guide cut), 2026-03-05 -6.99% (FY2026 range first issued), 2025-10-30 +22.89% (raise plus buyback). FY reaffirmed on 2026-07-30 closed -2.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Barchart on 2026-07-30 already called the FY guide 'optimistic', and consensus at about $440m sits $10m under the midpoint. If the market feared a cut below the low end, the stock would not be up about 4% over 20 days and 13.6% over the month into the print with shorts covering. The unpriced piece is how far below $115m a Q4 guide could land without an acquisition.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list since 2026-07-01 shows no 8-K after 2026-07-30 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001743725&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40). The 10-Q gives Ekumen's terms (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001743725/000174372526000021/gdyn-20260630.htm). FY consensus around $440m is search-snippet only and disputed ($447.7m on Chartmill).

findings.finding: Two peers spoke after GDYN and lowered or trimmed outlooks. Infosys (2026-10-23) set FY27 cc growth at 1-2%, citing heightened volatility. Cognizant (today, 2026-10-29 bmo) narrowed 2026 cc growth to 4.0-4.4%, revenue $22.05-22.14bn against $22.04-22.35bn in July, with Q3 bookings -7% y/y and organic growth under 1%. The offset is that Cognizant's Financial Services grew 12.0% and Communications/Media/Tech 10.5%, GDYN's two largest verticals after TMT.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GDYN-specific history on peer reads. GDYN fell -16.44% on 2025-07-31, a guide cut into a weak IT-services tape.
findings.why_not_priced: Cognizant printed this morning; GDYN's close today has only partly absorbed it. Infosys has had a week. A proxy, not GDYN's own number. GDYN is a digital-engineering name whose AI revenue grew over 50% y/y, so transmission is weak.
findings.independence: Infosys 6-K 2026-10-23 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000044/exv99w01.htm) is a separate document pointing the same way. Proxy only.

findings.finding: Accenture's fiscal Q4 2026 (2026-10-01): revenue $18.68bn, +7% local currency, above its guide; record 141 bookings over $100m; book-to-bill 1.2. Shares rose about 19% on the day after a 32% YTD drop on AI-disruption fears. This is the sector rerating GDYN has ridden over the month.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: GDYN is +13.6% over the month against +3.7% for peers (StockStory 2026-10-28). What remains is only that the AI-disruption discount on IT services has eased.
findings.independence: Benzinga/finviz coverage of the move (https://finviz.com/news/397737/accenture-shares-rise-after-fourth-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-beat-estimates). Proxy, and it points against the Cognizant/Infosys finding.

findings.finding: The $50m buyback authorized 2025-10-23 had only $19.2m left at 2026-06-30 after 4.4m shares were bought for $28.8m in H1 (2.6m for $17.3m in Q2). At Q2's pace it would be nearly used up by Q3-end. The original authorization came with the Q3'25 print, so a renewal or upsizing alongside this print is plausible. Cash is $298.4m against a market cap of about $710m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-30, the print after the authorization, +22.89%; that print also carried a guide raise, so the buyback's share of the move cannot be separated.
findings.why_not_priced: Remaining authorization is a 10-Q footnote; no preview mentions a renewal. If the market expected a new authorization, it would show in previews or a pre-print bid, and neither is visible. This is an inference that a program near exhaustion gets renewed, not a stated plan.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript gives the same repurchase figures (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/grid-dynamics-gdyn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); same company source.

findings.finding: Concentration is rising. Customer 1 was 17.4% of Q2 revenue (15.1% a year earlier), top 5 were 43.5% (37.5%), top 10 were 61.5% (57.3%). Management flagged volatility at a top-30-to-40 client and sensitivity in brick-and-mortar retail (26.5% of revenue, -0.7% y/y). Net of the rest: TMT, 31.8% of revenue, grew 36.4% y/y, so a retail or finance soft spot is offset unless the top client itself slows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-07-31 -16.44% guide cut was tied to client-specific softness. No later print isolates the line.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-Q, so the level is known. What is unknown is whether a top client moved in Q3, and no counterparty source was found. A known risk with no new evidence.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, top-5/top-10 and retail commentary (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/30/grid-dynamics-gdyn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/); same company, two documents.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The stock ran +4% over 20 days (+13.6% over the month per StockStory) with shorts covering, so the beat is expected and the slightly negative guidance lean cuts mildly against the run-up. That keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 6: the beat-pattern finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4. This name sold its last beat (-2.41%), and a ~$114m print lands inside the company's own $112-114m guide.
Lesson 3: the FY-guide finding moved from -1.0 to -0.8, because its own caveat (street FY around $440m already sits in the lower half) has to reach the number.
Lesson 5: the Accenture proxy cut from +0.3 to +0.2, since the month's sector rerating already carries it. The Cognizant/Infosys proxy stays at -0.5, filed as a proxy.
Lesson 9: the concentration finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2, net of TMT (31.8% of revenue) growing 36% y/y.
Lessons 5 and 7: the short-interest covering finding stays small (-0.2 to -0.1); the insider 10b5-1 sale goes to 0.0. No crowded short, so no squeeze adjustment on the negatives.
